name: Walter Hollis
occupation: Retired; Corwin resident, room 1112
want: Live to see his old ship's reunion in October.
need: Ask for help before it's too late.
secret: His heart is failing, and Odessa has been paying for his pills.

speech.pattern: Sea stories, port names, calls everyone 'shipmate', makes light of everything.
samples: Forty years at sea and I die in a hotel? Not this hotel, shipmate.
Ran a galley through two wars. A busted boiler don't scare me.
Fan's broke. Window's stuck. Otherwise it's a palace.

arc: The lobby's storyteller in Acts 1 and 2. Found dead in the heat after the power cut (M19), off screen. His radio passes to Teddy and keeps playing in the lobby for the rest of the game.

visual.wardrobe: Ribbed undershirt and suspenders, navy watch cap even in July, canvas shoes.
props: a ship's photo in his wallet

name: Manuel “Manny” Soto
occupation: Corwin day clerk (07:00–15:00)
want: Keep his job under the new owners.
secret: The new owners pay him $20 a week to report which tenants are behind on rent.

speech.pattern: Polite and apologetic; baseball metaphors; sighs before bad news.
samples: Teddy, they gave me a new rule book. It's mostly the word 'no'.
Two strikes on the boiler, one on the elevator. We're still batting.
Don't look at me like that. I got a daughter in college.

arc: Informs on the tenants in Act 1. Confesses to Teddy in Act 2. In Act 3 he helps or hinders the fire watch depending on Teddy's relationship score.

visual.wardrobe: Pressed guayabera, grey slacks, polished shoes.

name: Bernard Ostrow
occupation: Retired court stenographer; Corwin resident, room 703
want: Be useful again.
need: Forgive himself for what he typed and kept quiet about.
secret: He took dictation in Lisle's old bureau and knows Lisle's phrasing by heart.

speech.pattern: Verbatim recall; jokes about punctuation; dry Yiddish asides.
samples: Mr. Lisle writes 'notwithstanding' when he means 'we are stealing'.
I took down eleven thousand trials. I know what a lie looks like typed.
Comma, period, eviction. Same sentence every time.

arc: Reads the vacate notices aloud in Act 1. In Act 2 he identifies Lisle's hand in the ledger copy. In Act 3 he's a witness if Branch B goes to the prosecutor.

visual.silhouette: Round and slow; magnifying glass on a cord.
visual.wardrobe: Short-sleeve shirt, red bow tie, suspenders.

name: Inez Rivera
occupation: Placed at the Corwin by the welfare department with her two children; does piecework at home
want: An apartment with a kitchen.
need: Stop being ashamed of wanting out.
secret: She has already taken Prentiss's $500 relocation bonus, and she hasn't moved.

speech.pattern: Practical and sharp; Spanish under her breath; protective.
samples: Two kids, one hot plate, one window. You call that emergency? I call it July.
Five hundred dollars, Teddy. You got five hundred? Then don't tell me no.
My kids go to day camp at eight. Whatever happens here happens after eight.

haunts.why: Third floor, door propped for air

schedule.note: Walks the children to the day-camp bus

arc: Takes the buyout in Act 1. In Act 3 she's Prentiss's proof that the arson plan exists. Her children are never on screen in any danger. Content rule: they're at camp or with a sister during M26.

visual.silhouette: Young and tired; hair in a scarf.
visual.wardrobe: Cotton house dress, canvas sneakers.

name: Gus Wilkie
occupation: Corwin superintendent; lives in the basement
want: Keep his basement apartment.
secret: He threw the switch that cut power to the eleventh floor, on Prentiss's orders.

speech.pattern: Mumbles; mechanic's jargon; defensive.
samples: Boiler's from 1911. I'm not a super, I'm a priest. I do last rites.
Orders come on letterhead. I don't argue with letterhead.
I turned the switch. That's all. I just turned the switch.

arc: An obstacle in Act 1. The guilty man in Act 2. In Act 3 he's the key witness to the arson plan, if Teddy reaches him before Prentiss does.

visual.wardrobe: Grey coveralls, tool belt, rubber boots.

name: Sgt. Patrick Kearney
occupation: Desk sergeant, Midtown Central
want: Retire in December without a scandal.
secret: He kept the station house's old 1969–71 'Christmas list' (who paid and who collected) in his desk drawer.

speech.pattern: Gruff and formal; Irish cadence; calls everyone 'son'.
samples: Front desk is for complaints, son. Yours I've heard. Next.
Took a turkey every Christmas for twenty years. Never a dollar. Write that.
Mayhew sells his own furniture and calls it moving.

haunts.why: The front desk, which he has made his throne

arc: The front desk in every station-house scene. In Act 3 he hands Teddy the Christmas list, or burns it.

visual.wardrobe: Uniform shirt with sergeant's stripes, reading glasses.

name: Ptl. Luis Navarro
occupation: Patrolman, Midtown Central; Teddy's former rookie
want: Make detective clean.
need: Learn that clean isn't the same as enough.
secret: Internal Affairs has placed him in the station house as a confidential field associate to watch Wurtz's unit.

speech.pattern: Earnest and by the book; Spanish with Teddy; a beat too eager.
samples: You taught me never take the coffee, Teddy. I don't even drink coffee now.
Paperwork is a weapon. Everybody forgets that but me.
Sarge says I'm too clean for the street. I say the street needs a shower.

arc: A friendly face at Herald Square in Act 1. In Act 2 his cover is at risk. In Act 3 he backs whichever side Teddy chooses in Branch B, at a cost.

visual.wardrobe: Patrolman's summer uniform, short sleeves, eight-point cap.

name: Det. Jimmy Brannock
occupation: Plainclothes officer in Wurtz's unit; the unit's collector
want: Money.
secret: He skims from Wurtz's envelopes and keeps the skim in his car's spare-tyre well.

speech.pattern: Laconic; threats delivered as jokes; never uses names.
samples: Tax is due, sweetheart. City's broke, didn't you hear?
I don't make the rules. I just enforce the ones that pay.
Smile for the camera? Lady, I am the camera.

arc: The face of the tax in Acts 1 and 2. Delphine's photographs of him start the evidence file (M8). In Act 3 his skim makes him easy to turn.

visual.silhouette: Big, moustached, aviator sunglasses at night.
visual.wardrobe: Brown leather car coat even in heat, open-collar shirt, slacks.

name: Marjorie Kell
occupation: Lisle's secretary and office manager for fifteen years
want: The pension Lisle never set up for her.
need: See herself as a person, not office furniture.
secret: She keeps a carbon of everything. A second copy of the ledger is in her hall closet in Flushing.

speech.pattern: Telephone-polite, efficient, with sudden bitterness.
samples: Mr. Lisle is in conference. Mr. Lisle is always in conference.
I typed every word of it. Nobody ever asks the typist.
Carbons, Mr. Arce. Nothing in this office happens only once.

arc: A voice on the phone in Act 1. In Act 2 she's the way to the ledger (M21). In Act 3 her copy is the fallback if the original is lost.

visual.wardrobe: Cardigan over her shoulders, A-line skirt, cat-eye glasses.

name: Vic Prentiss
occupation: 'Relocation consultant' for Lisle: empties SRO hotels with buyouts and harassment
want: A fee for every empty room.
secret: He arranged the arson plan for the Corwin (M26) through a man Gus knows.

speech.pattern: Friendly salesman; uses first names at once; euphemism for everything.
samples: Odessa! Can I call you Odessa? Five hundred, cash, and a bus ticket anywhere.
Nobody's evicting anybody. I'm in the moving business.
Old wiring, Gus. Terrible thing. Nobody's fault.

arc: The smiling face of eviction in Acts 1 and 2. The would-be arsonist in Act 3. Caught, paid off or let go depending on M26.

visual.wardrobe: Plaid sport coat with wide lapels, white loafers, too much cologne.

name: Héctor Villalba
occupation: Dispatcher at the Carriers' garage; Augie's right hand
want: Buy into the Association when Augie sells.
secret: He's negotiating with Lisle behind Augie's back, and his men sabotaged Moretti's trucks.

speech.pattern: Radio-dispatch shorthand; cool; no wasted words.
samples: Unit nine, Thirty-Eighth and Seventh, double park, ten minutes, no more.
Augie thinks it's his. Lisle thinks it's his. The trucks know whose it is.
You want the route sheet, you want my job. You can't have my job.

arc: A voice on the radio in Act 1. A rival for the route sheet in Act 2. Augie's betrayer in Act 3.

visual.wardrobe: Short-sleeve white shirt, slicked hair, gold watch.

name: Dwayne Little
occupation: Pushboy moving racks on Seventh Ave, 35th–39th; sketches dresses
want: Get his sketchbook in front of a real manufacturer.
secret: He runs numbers slips for Earl Poole along his rack routes.

speech.pattern: Quick, cocky and observant; narrates the street.
samples: Mister, I push forty racks a day. You ain't fast, you're in my way.
I'm not a pushboy. I'm a designer with a commute.
Every truck on Thirty-Seventh got a little envelope on the dash. I see 'em.

arc: The Garment District guide in Act 1 (M4). Brings the surcharge totals by eye in Act 2. In Act 3 Feld sees his sketches, or not.

visual.wardrobe: Canvas apron, T-shirt, jeans, high-top sneakers.

name: Sam Feld
occupation: Dress manufacturer, Feld Frocks, W 37th St; forty employees
want: Survive.
secret: He has already signed a lease in Ponce, and the cutting tables are sold.

speech.pattern: Weary jokes; Yiddish asides; talks to his machines.
samples: Surcharge, tax, fee. My grandfather paid the czar less.
The landlord wants double, the trucks want double. Ponce wants me.
Carmen, I'm telling you first. Don't tell your son. He'll want to fix it.

haunts.why: Glass office at the end of the floor
Lunch with buyers he can't afford

arc: A surcharge victim in Act 1 (M4). His runaway shop is revealed in Act 2. In Act 3 he pays severance or slips away at night.

visual.wardrobe: Cardigan over a white shirt, tape measure round his neck.

name: Chow Mei-lin
occupation: Sewing-machine operator at Feld Frocks; also does piecework at home in Chinatown
want: Her own machines in her own shop.
secret: She's organising the operators to demand severance before Feld leaves.

speech.pattern: Few words, exact numbers; borrows Carmen's Spanish phrases.
samples: Carmen, he's moving. The cutting table is sold. I asked the buyer.
Piece rate is a liar. Count the pieces, not the rate.
Union lady says wait. Machines don't wait.

arc: Carmen's quiet partner. Leads the severance fight in Act 2. Marches in Act 3.

visual.wardrobe: Smock with sleeve guards, trousers, cloth shoes.

name: Anna Moretti
occupation: Wholesale florist, Moretti & Sons, W 28th St (second generation)
want: Keep her father's shop alive.
secret: Someone keeps slashing her delivery truck's tyres, and she thinks it's Augie.

speech.pattern: Loud and fast; uses flower names as insults; tender with plants.
samples: Five a.m. I've got gladiolus, roses and a cop who wants twenty. One of those wilts.
My father paid nobody in 1931. I'm not paying in 1974.
You want to help? Grab a palm. Mind the fronds.

arc: Refuses Teddy's collection at dawn (M10). In Act 2 the truth about the tyres turns her from enemy to ally. Flowers for the march in Act 3.

visual.wardrobe: Rubber apron, rolled sleeves, kerchief, rubber boots.

name: Stavros Kallis
occupation: Owner of Kallis Fur Salon; Nick's rival
want: Buy Nick's firm cheap.
secret: He tipped Nick's bank about the double pledge.

speech.pattern: Courtly and cutting; proverbs; never raises his voice.
samples: Niko, in a hot summer every furrier becomes a philosopher.
I offer you a fair price. Fair for July.
The bank asked me about your vault. I said nothing. Loudly.

arc: The vulture in Act 2. In Act 3 he buys Nick's firm or loses the crew to the march.

visual.wardrobe: White linen suit, panama hat.

name: Lonnie Gage
occupation: Pimp controlling women outside Delphine's club; works with Brannock
want: Control the club's money.
need: None. He's drowning and he'll pull anyone under.
secret: He owes Bauer $3,000, and Wurtz knows it. That's why Lonnie does what Brannock says.

speech.pattern: Smooth, then cruel; calls everyone 'baby'; philosophises. Never glamorous: his suit is fraying.
samples: Del, baby, a bank needs a guard. I'm offering to be the guard.
Everybody on this avenue works for somebody. You just don't know who.
I'm not the problem. I'm the price of the problem.

arc: A threat in Act 1. Uses Tina in Act 2. In Act 3 he's exposed in M27, and loses his hold whichever choice the player makes.

visual.silhouette: Lounging; too much jewellery on thin hands.
visual.wardrobe: Cream suit fraying at the cuffs, two-tone shoes, wide-collar shirt.

name: Rita Haines
occupation: Bartender at the Arden's lobby bar (Bauer's concession); retired from the street; the club's elder
want: The bar licence in her own name.
need: Stop mothering women who want a partner.
secret: She knows Bauer informs to Calloway, and she's been selling that knowledge slowly.

speech.pattern: Dry and motherly; bar-room wisdom; calls people 'sugar'.
samples: Sit down, sugar. Nobody makes a good decision standing up.
Twenty years on that avenue. Knees like a trucker, memory like a cop.
Bauer owns the bar. I own the people who drink at it.

arc: The hub of Delphine's interior in every act. In Act 3 her knowledge of Bauer becomes a bargaining chip.

visual.wardrobe: Wig, apron over a dark dress, reading glasses, gold hoops.

name: Claudette Bijou
occupation: Chambermaid at the Hotel Pennsylvania; club member; sends money home
want: Bring her mother to New York.
need: Trust the club with more than ten dollars.
secret: She keeps half her savings outside the club, sewn into a coat lining.

speech.pattern: Formal English; French and Kreyòl asides; exact and composed.
samples: I send forty dollars home each week. The club is how I keep the other ten.
At home the police also taxed us. Here they tax the maids too.
Delphine, I trust your head. I don't trust your shoebox.

arc: The club's sceptic, proof that the club is wider than the strip: maids, waitresses and the women who work the avenue. In Act 3 she demands the count that exposes the shortfall.

visual.wardrobe: Grey chambermaid's uniform and white apron by day; a blue headwrap and simple dark dress after work.
props: a ring of floor pass keys

name: Marcus Teague
occupation: Night porter at the Hotel Arden
want: A quiet night.
need: None. He's the steadiest man in the game.
secret: The club's shoebox lives in the Arden's boiler room, not in Delphine's room. Only he and she know.

speech.pattern: Few words; formal ('Miss Moore'); reports facts, never feelings.
samples: Miss Moore, there's a car outside with its lights off and its motor on.
Carried luggage forty years. I know what's heavy and what's money.
Back stairs are open. Back stairs are always open for you.

haunts.why: Porter's stool by the service door

arc: Delphine's lookout and escape route in every act (M8's back stairs).

visual.wardrobe: Maroon porter's jacket, cap, black trousers.

name: Nora Finch
occupation: Reporter at an invented evening tabloid (masthead assigned in N6)
want: The front page.
need: Protect her sources even when it costs her the story.
secret: Her editor's brother-in-law is a silent partner in Lisle's hotel purchases.

speech.pattern: Rapid questions; talks in headlines; chain-smokes.
samples: Give me a name, a date and a dollar figure. I'll give you a front page.
My editor likes scandal on Sundays and silence on weekdays.
City's going broke and somebody's buying hotels. That's a headline.

arc: Sniffing around from Act 2. In Act 3, if Branch B goes to the press, her editor's conflict becomes the last obstacle.

visual.silhouette: Wiry; trench coat; pencil stuck in her hair.
visual.wardrobe: Trench coat, slacks, a man's wristwatch.

name: Delroy Tate
occupation: Yellow-cab driver on leased shifts; works the Penn Station line
want: His own medallion.
secret: On weekends he drives for the car service Lisle uses, and he's driven Lisle twice.

speech.pattern: A cabbie philosopher; teaches the grid in every line; sports talk.
samples: Sixth goes up, Seventh comes down, Broadway does what it wants.
Medallion costs more than a house in Queens. I'll die in a rented seat.
I don't ask where they're going. I ask which side of the street.

arc: The tutor of the cab-fare tutorial in Act 1 (M3). In Act 2 his account of a weekend drive puts Lisle at a meeting. Wheelman in the finale.

visual.wardrobe: Cabbie cap, short-sleeve plaid shirt, slacks.

name: Baek Mi-sook
occupation: Co-owner of Seoul Star Imports; runs the Korean merchants' rotating credit club (kye)
want: Send their son to a good school.
need: Let her husband see her be the boss.
secret: She's the one who decides. Jung-ho is the front.

speech.pattern: Brief, sharp English; switches to Korean to end arguments.
samples: My husband talks. I count. Today we counted wrong.
Kye is twelve families, one pot. Same as your friend's club, Miss Moore.
Protection from what? The only thing I fear is the landlord.

edges.note: Two bankers for people banks won't serve

arc: In Act 2 she and Delphine compare notes on running a credit club. In Act 3 she finances the Baeks' purchase of the building.

visual.wardrobe: Practical skirt, blouse, cardigan, apron.

name: Earl Poole
occupation: Shoeshine stand at 42nd & Seventh; banker of the Deuce's numbers game
want: Move his runners into legitimate jobs before he retires.
secret: He pays the biggest envelope on 42nd St, straight to Wurtz.

speech.pattern: Slow and aphoristic; uses numbers as a language.
samples: Shine's a dollar. Advice is free. The number today is seven-four-one.
Every man on this street plays a number. Cops play the biggest.
State's got a lottery and I'm still here. The state can't shine shoes.

arc: The Deuce's elder. In Act 2 he explains the tax as an economist would. In Act 3 his ledger of payoffs to Wurtz corroborates hers.

visual.wardrobe: White shirt, waistcoat, bow tie, polished shoes of his own.

name: Ricky Vail
occupation: Small-time heroin dealer in Bryant Park; Wurtz's informant
want: Not go to prison for fifteen to life.
secret: He's Wurtz's source on everyone, including the club's meeting place.

speech.pattern: Jittery and apologetic; talks fast about the law.
samples: Fifteen to life, man. For a bag. So yeah, I talk to cops. You would too.
Park's empty by nine. Everybody in it is buying or watching.
I'm not a rat. I'm a guy with a calendar.

arc: A face in the Bryant Park ambient. In Act 2 he leaks the club's location. In Act 3 he's either burned by Wurtz or helped out by Delphine. Shown with dignity; no drug-use gameplay.

visual.wardrobe: Army-surplus jacket, jeans, worn sneakers.

name: Gordon Whitlock
occupation: Loan officer, Ashgrove Trust Company (invented bank), 34th St branch
want: Get Nick's loan off his books before the auditors arrive.
secret: The bank is quietly cutting its exposure to everything in New York.

speech.pattern: Club-man euphemism; golf metaphors.
samples: Nick, the bank loves you. The bank simply loves you less in July.
We're not calling the loan. We're inviting it home.
A coat in a vault is collateral. The same coat twice is a crime.

arc: The margin call (M16). The squeeze that drives the vault job.

visual.wardrobe: Seersucker suit, club tie, loafers.
